entries.name: Grain farm barn and silo
entries.description: Low muted-burgundy timber grain barn, one separate broad slate-blue cylindrical grain silo, and a small open lean-to. The barn footprint is approximately 12m by 8m and its eaves 4m high, ridge 6m; the silo is 9m high. One clearly measured 2.1m personnel door and one broad 4.2m loading opening. Quiet grass around a simple worn farmyard patch. No grain fields.

entries.name: Dairy barn and milk tank
entries.description: Long pale-plaster dairy barn approximately 15m by 7m, 4m eaves, 6m ridge, muted terracotta roof, and one broad low cylindrical silver milk tank beside a small milking shelter. One ordinary 2.1m personnel door and two broad 4.2m agricultural openings. Quiet grass and compact worn farmyard patch. No pasture fields.

entries.name: Produce shed and broad greenhouse
entries.description: One low muted-timber produce shed approximately 7m by 6m and one unmistakable broad glazed greenhouse approximately 10m by 8m. The greenhouse has only a few thick simple structural divisions and soft muted-glass panes. Shed eaves 3m, ridge 4.5m, with one 2.1m personnel door and one broad loading opening. Quiet worn yard grass. No vegetable rows or produce-dot textures.

entries.name: Orchard packing barn and produce shelter
entries.description: Low pale-plaster packing shed approximately 11m by 7m, 3m eaves, 5m ridge, muted terracotta broad pitched roof, a small open packing shelter and three large simple produce bins in restrained ochre/foliage masses. One ordinary 2.1m personnel door. Quiet grass and worn loading patch. No orchard trees, fruit dots, planting rows or fine crate grids.

entries.name: Livestock stable and feeding shelter
entries.description: Broad low L-shaped timber stable approximately 14m by 10m at its extent, 3.5m eaves, 5.5m ridge, subdued slate roof and one small open feeding shelter with broad ochre hay mass. One ordinary 2.1m personnel door and broad agricultural opening. Quiet farmyard grass. No paddock field, surrounding fence or animals.

job.direction: FARM BUILDING CORE CAMERA CORRECTION. Create a COMPLETELY NEW clean farm core family from the supplied exact 2:1 construction guide and current canonical painted style. Use the guide middle panel for the 2×2 tier. Copy its exact shallow dimetric angle, ground axes, human proportions and muted semantic colours into the new painted barns. The guide is the only image reference; do not copy its flat reference cuboid, its diagram labels or its person. Five occupied cells only in 3 columns by 2 rows, row-major order, slot 6 empty. Each square cell is one registered 2×2 tile 32m farm core cutout inside an independently rendered 5×5 tile farm field plot. Do not duplicate fields or build a full 5 tile farm in these sprites. All architecture lies in a maximum 20m square envelope, whose ground projection is 213.33px wide by 106.67px high in normalized 256 cell: exact vertices (128,138.667),(234.667,192),(128,245.333),(21.333,192). Actual farmyard ground centre stays (128,192). Every wall baseline, barn roof eave, ridge, greenhouse base and canopy beam follows slope +0.500 or -0.500 precisely; vertical edges stay vertical. Every ground line must be visibly twice as wide as it is tall, with a shallow slope of 0.500, not a steep isometric angle. Preserve true world scale: 2.1m door 11.2px high, 0.95m door 5.07px wide, 3m storey 16px, 4.2m loading bay 22.4px in normalized 256 cell. At a 512px source cell these values double. Center grass worn patches around measured farmyard centre, never around alpha extent. Keep ground patches quiet and light with irregular soft grassy edges and NO thick diamond platform, no soil walls, no opaque full parcel card. Preserve generous transparency and gutters. Reduce noise drastically: broad readable barn masses and silos/greenhouses are identity; no tiny roof ribbing, fine window mullions, wood scratches, exposed hay dots, railings, bush fringes or gravel texture. Every family uses the same semantic muted palette and same upright physical scale. Render five farmyards on a genuinely transparent sheet, no labels, gridlines, guide strokes or palette cards in final output. Clean broad flat brush shapes only. Tiny textures and bright saturated greens or bright red roofs are prohibited. NO trees and NO bushes. Barely visible simple grass patch under each barn group, feathered irregular perimeter, no garden border or crisp full-square diamond. The barns, silo, greenhouse and packing shelter must remain broad and recognizable at thumbnail size. Sheet width-to-height 3:2, square cells, ample separation.

prompt:
Fixed orthographic 2:1 dimetric camera: ground edges at +26.565 and -26.565 degrees, vertical walls, two visible facades, no perspective convergence.
Lock every building, roof ridge, garden boundary, fence, court and yard to the same two ground axes. No in-plot yaw, diagonal rotation, camera tilt or camera rotation. An alternate entrance orientation swaps the two grid axes; it never rotates a building off-grid.
Quiet hand-painted miniature architecture with clean silhouettes, broad roof and wall colour masses, restrained warm materials, northwest daylight and soft contact shadows.
A consistent world scale: one tile is 16 metres square. A person is 1.75m tall; ordinary personnel doors are 2.1m high and 0.95m wide; storeys are 3m; windows are about 1.2m high; low fences are 1.2m. Vehicle loading bays are 4.2m high and visibly distinct from personnel doors.
Bigger buildings gain additional rooms, wings, floors and repeated bays at the SAME human scale. Never enlarge doors, windows, people, garden fences or benches to fill a bigger parcel.
Designed to remain recognizable at Region 0.5x and Town 1x: distinctive roofline, clear facade shading, a few large openings and broad planted clusters. No individual bricks, roof tiles, woodgrain scratches, tiny lettering, tiny flower dots, dense crate grids, fine handrails, thin window mullions or decorative speckle.
Preserve useful large identifiers such as loading sheds, silos, greenhouses, chimneys, awnings and sports surfaces. No people as decorative scale filler, no text or logos.
Use the supplied semantic muted material swatches across all families; maintain broad light and shaded facades within those hues. Give each identity a distinct roofline or one large identifying mass, with restrained slate, terracotta, foliage, ochre or burgundy accents. Recognition at Town size must come from silhouette and broad colour blocks, not tiny ornaments or texture.
Genuine transparent background, isolated complete sprites with generous transparent gutters. No scenery outside the parcel, no backdrop cards or opaque plinth. Gardens blend with the climate terrain.
Production 3x2 atlas, exactly 6 slots in row-major order; each cell is a registered architectural cutout at the stated parcel scale, not a close-up of the building. Follow each slot's parcel-to-cell calibration: equal footprints share one pixel-to-metre scale; larger footprints have proportionally smaller doors in the normalized cell so they render at the same world height. Do not give different footprint tiers equal door pixel heights. Do not independently fit each building's bounding box.
Physical ground registration in every 256px square cell: parcel centre is (128.0,192.0), independent of alpha bounds, shadows, roof height and planting. Around that centre project east/north/up metres with x=(east-north)*2 and y=(east+north)-height*2 in world pixels, then multiply by 256/(48*footprint). The inset architectural/garden envelope is at most 10m*footprint square; its exact 2:1 ground vertices are (128.0,138.7), (234.7,192.0), (128.0,245.3), (21.3,192.0). The full 16m*footprint parcel is native world terrain and extends beyond this cutout cell; do not shrink its physical metre scale or paint a full-parcel opaque diamond to fit the cell. Register the actual ground centre, never the silhouette bottom or contact-shadow extremity. Keep all complete architecture and planting inside the transparent cell with filtering gutters.
Warm dusty sand, pale stone and plaster, terracotta and sparse dry planting; preserve every physical dimension.
Canonical desert material swatches: plaster #e3d7b7; stone #c7bca5; brick #b1846c; timber #997a5b; slate #697780; terracotta #a76f51; glass #769493; metal #6c7878; ink #4b5954; cream #f0e9d6; ochre #c2a269; burgundy #996b63; paving #cdc6ae; path #d8cfb2; water #658f9c; ground #c6b48b; foliage #899265. These are restrained painted colour targets, with soft light/shade variation, not saturated replacements.
